QuestionStmt.S: A null point is obtained at 200 cm on potentiometer wire when cell in secondary circuit is shunted by $5\Omega$. When a resistance of $15\Omega$ is used for shunting, null point moves to 300 cm. The internal resistance of the cell is

Solution.S:
Let the internal resistance of the cell be $r$. The balancing length is proportional to the terminal potential difference of the cell.

When shunted with resistance $R_s$, the terminal voltage is:
$$V = \frac{R_s}{R_s + r} E$$

Since balancing length $l \propto V$, we have:
$$\frac{l_1}{l_2} = \frac{V_1}{V_2} = \frac{R_{s1}/(R_{s1} + r)}{R_{s2}/(R_{s2} + r)}$$

Given $l_1 = 200$ cm, $R_{s1} = 5\Omega$, $l_2 = 300$ cm, $R_{s2} = 15\Omega$.

$$\frac{200}{300} = \frac{5/(5 + r)}{15/(15 + r)} = \frac{5}{5 + r} \times \frac{15 + r}{15}$$

$$\frac{2}{3} = \frac{5(15 + r)}{15(5 + r)} = \frac{75 + 5r}{75 + 15r}$$

Cross-multiply:
$$2(75 + 15r) = 3(75 + 5r)$$
$$150 + 30r = 225 + 15r$$
$$30r - 15r = 225 - 150$$
$$15r = 75 \quad \Rightarrow \quad r = 5\Omega$$

Thus the internal resistance is $5\Omega$, which corresponds to option C.
